chunks: Salih ibn 'Uqba from Nasr ibn Qabous from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The feeding of a believer is more beloved to me than freeing ten necks and ten Hajj pilgrimages. I said, 'Ten necks and ten Hajj?' He said, 'O Nasr! If you do not feed him, he will die, or you will direct him (elsewhere) so he comes to a Nasibi (Hostile one) and asks him; and death is better for him than asking a Nasibi. O Nasr! The one who revives a believer, it is as if he has revived all the people. So if you do not feed him, you have caused him to die, and if you feed him, you have revived him.'

key_terms.نَاصِبٍ: Nasibi (Hostile one, specifically to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of feeding a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates feeding a believer above freeing ten slaves and performing ten Hajj pilgrimages, highlighting its critical role in preserving dignity and preventing spiritual decline. He illustrates that neglecting to feed a believer effectively causes their death, while providing sustenance is akin to reviving all of humanity, a concept rooted in the Shia tradition of sustaining the community against external pressures like the Nasibi. This act is thus framed not merely as charity, but as a vital mechanism for maintaining the believer's presence and status within the faith.

en.hubeali:
Salih Bin Uqba, from Nasr Bin Qabous, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The feeding of a Momin is more beloved to measws than freeing ten necks and performing ten Hajj’. I said, ‘Ten necks and ten Hajj?’ So heasws said: ‘O Nasr! If you do not feed him, he would either die, or you would have indicated him (to go elsewhere), so he would go to a Hostile one (Nasibi) and ask him; and the death would be better for him than asking a Hostile one (Nasibi). O Nasr! The one who revives a Momin, so it is as if he has revived the people altogether. So if you do not feed him, so you have caused him to died, and if you do feed him, so you have revived him’.
en.sarwar: 20. Salih ibn ‘Aqabah has narrated from Nasr ibn Qabus from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Feeding a believer is, indeed, more beloved to me than setting free ten slaves and performing ten Hajj.’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘Is it like setting free ten slaves and performing ten Hajj?’ He has said that the Imam said, ‘O Nasr, if you do not feed him he will die or you will humiliate him, then he will go to one who is a bitter enemy of the Imam and will ask him for help. Death is better for him than asking help from such enemy of the Imam. O Nasr, giving life to a believer is like giving life to all mankind. If you do not feed him you have caused his death, if you feed him you have given him life.’”
